newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Commission installed to run Liberian elections.
newsitem.headline: Commission installed to run Liberian elections.

text.p: Liberia installed a seven-member independent commission on Wednesday to run elections next month after seven years of civil war in the West African nation, witnesses said.

The Independent Elections Commission, sworn in by interim head of state Ruth Perry, is headed by Henry Andrews, a veteran Liberian journalist in his 50s. It includes three non-voting international members.

"The Independent Elections Commission is charged to ensure that elections are held on 30th May, 1997," declared Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi, whose country leads the West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG policing Liberia since 1990.
"We believe that this date is realisable and it is obtainable," Ikimi said at the ceremony held inside Monrovia's Executive Mansion presidential complex.

Two of Liberia's leading warlords blamed for the civil war which killed more than 150,000 people but who are now running for president -- Charles Taylor and George Boley -- attended. A third warlord and rival candidate, Alhaji Kromah, was absent.
